Date: 2028-03-30T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + three asks on prompt/output handling

Hi Emily — thanks again for the demo and the thoughtful questions today. Short recap and immediate asks so we can keep procurement moving.

1) What we demoed: hosted inference with optional prompt-output logging for quality; prefix/KV caching for session performance; can pin region and model.
2) You flagged: (a) state residency requirements, (b) maximum retention for prompt/response content that may contain PHI, and (c) evidence for our controls (SOC2/dataflow).

Could you confirm three items so we can produce a targeted response from engineering/security?
- Which regulatory bucket does Acadia need us to satisfy for residency (US-only, particular states)?
- Do you have a maximum TTL for prompt outputs that contain PHI (e.g., 30 / 90 days)?
- Are you looking for a short evidence bundle (SOC2 summary + dataflow + TTL table) or a formal security questionnaire?

Attaching the meeting recording and a short product note: redwood-acadia-demo.mp4 (video).

Next steps: once we get those answers Hannah will return a field-level table (what we store, where, TTL) and attach the SOC2 summary and dataflow diagram.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132
From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@acadiahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acadiahealth.com
Date: 2028-03-31T09:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + three asks on prompt/output handling

Jordan — great meeting, thanks. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency: Acadia requires US-only data residency; for some datasets we need physical storage in our contract to be in the continental US (we generally accept east/west regions).
- Retention: For any prompt/response content that may contain PHI or 18 identifiers, our security policy default is a max of 90 days. We can consider a shorter window for more sensitive flows.
- Evidence: please send a short evidence bundle first (SOC2 Type II summary + dataflow diagram + a small table mapping prompt field -> stored? -> location -> TTL). If that aligns we'll follow with a one-page questionnaire if needed.

Example of the table we need (one row per field):
- field name / prompt or response? / persisted by Redwood? (yes/no) / storage region / TTL if persisted

We also attached our internal checklist (acadia-security-checklist.xlsx) — it lists a couple more asks (encryption at rest keys, KMS integration, and auditable logs).

Emily Stone
Director, Product Security | Acadia Health
emily.stone@acadiahealth.com

Emily — thanks for the clarity and the checklist. Apologies for the slight delay; below is the field-level mapping and a short description of controls and residency. I've attached a SOC2 summary and a dataflow diagram as requested (redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, redwood_dataflow-diagram.svg) plus a short privacy appendix.

Field-level mapping (high level):
- end_user_free_text_prompt / prompt / persisted by Redwood? -> by default: NO (ephemeral in serving layer). If customer enables prompt-output logging for quality/analytics we persist a copy in secure object storage. / storage region -> US-east (Ashburn) or US-west on request / TTL when persisted -> configurable; default retention for logged prompt text = 30 days; max configurable window for enterprise customers = 90 days (policy enforced via MSA)
- assistant_generated_response / response / persisted? -> by default: NO. If logging enabled we persist output for quality and traceability / storage region -> US-east / TTL -> default 30 days; enterprise option to reduce to 0 days or to 7 days for higher-sensitivity flows
- session_KV_cache (model context) / internal transient cache / persisted? -> NO (in-memory only; not written to disk). Cached KV is lost with instance restarts and not included in logs unless explicitly captured via logging opt-in.
- request_metadata (timestamp, model, latency, token counts) / persisted? -> YES, aggregated logs and traces are retained for troubleshooting / storage region -> US-east / TTL -> 90 days by default for enterprise contracts (retention can be shortened on request)
- hashed_user_ids / pseudonymous identifiers / persisted? -> YES if customer chooses to send them; we store hashed values in encrypted object storage / storage region -> US-east / TTL -> 90 days default; can be reduced via config or contractual term

Controls and notes:
- Residency: we support region pinning to continental US only for Acadia; production data will be stored in US-East (Ashburn) by default. We do not replicate customer data outside the chosen region unless explicitly configured.
- Encryption: all persisted data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for enterprise plans; evidence included in attached privacy appendix.
- Audit & logs: We provide audit logs for account activity and request metadata. Full request payloads (prompt/response) are only part of the logs when the customer opts into prompt logging; otherwise payloads are ephemeral.
- SOC2: attached is our SOC2 Type II summary (redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf). For deeper evidence we can provide the full report under an NDA.

Attachments included: redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, redwood_dataflow-diagram.svg, redwood-privacy-appendix.pdf

Recommended next steps:
1) Confirm that US-east storage satisfies Acadia's residency need.
2) Decide whether Acadia wants prompt/response payloads logged for the pilot. If not, we will default to no persistence for payloads.
3) If Acadia requires the 90-day max retention for PHI, we will include the TTL in the MSA and enable enterprise retention controls.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call with your security team to walk the diagram and appendix.

— Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
